speeches.content:
I. Restatement of My Position  
We contend that Skkiru and Larhgan are star-crossed lovers “engaged to be married” whose forced roles as “beggar” and “high priestess” keep them apart, yet they remain devoted, hoping one day to reunite.  

II. Strong Textual Support for Mutual, Ongoing Love  

1. Larhgan’s Titles and Emotional Appeals Reveal Awareness and Affection  
  A. Quote: “my erstwhile fiancé … I hope that knowledge [of my fidelity] will inspire you to complete cooperation with Bbulas” (Transcriber’s Note).  
     – She still calls him fiancé and appeals to his patriotism, not ignorance or rival.  
  B. Quote: “I do not think I shall ever marry. I shall make the religious life my career.”  
     – She vows lifelong celibacy because of her love for him. A mere dupe would not renounce all other unions.  
  C. Quote: “All three of Larhgan’s eyes fuzzed with emotion … ‘I’m proud of you, Skkiru.’”  
     – Genuine pride, not suspicion, upon his visible obedience and sacrifice.  

2. Skkiru’s Subservience and Suffering Undermine “Secret Scheme” Theory  
  A. Quote: “You are not supposed to think. Leave all the thinking to me!” / Skkiru meekly replies, “Yes, Bbulas.”  
     – Obedience contradicts a conspirator’s boldness. He endangers himself by using forbidden gear only sparingly to “play” the native role (see below) rather than mount any overthrow.  
  B. Quote: “He could not reconcile himself to his beggarhood … hoped it wouldn’t reach his antennae—if he … psonk in front of Larhgan, it would be the final humiliation.”  
     – He fears public breakdown, not because he plans an imminent coup, but because every transgression risks permanent loss of her favor—evidence he lives for her approval within the charade.  
  C. “He lacked authority and opportunity: ‘He hadn’t even been allowed to help in planning the huts.’”  
     – Without planning rights or followers, any grand plan is impossible; he has no resources to overthrow a regime backed by the “new way of life” majority and powerful Earthmen.  

III. Refutation of Debater_B’s “Secret Scheme” Argument  

1. Limited Use of Land Transport Serves Performance, Not Overthrow  
  A. Quote: “primitive societies differ sharply … we have to be different to attract Earthmen.” / Skkiru’s pontooned mudshoes heighten his “beggar” authenticity.  
     – If he sought to impress Earthmen toward a coup, he would hide his advanced equipment rather than use it publicly. His use also incurs severe personal risk: “I hate Terra … I hate Terra.” Why risk discredit when his loyalty to Snaddra (and Larhgan) is professed?  

2. Chocolate Consumption Is Survival Strategy, Not Selfishness  
  A. Quote: “Chocolate increased the body’s resistance to weather.”  
     – As the only Beggar, he must endure horrid conditions to maintain the illusion for Earthmen and Larhgan’s continued hopes. Sacrificing the “offering” to his own body is necessary to play his part to the end (“for Snaddra” and “for Larhgan”), not mere self-interest.  

3. Larhgan’s Deference to Bbulas Because She Follows Duty, Not Ignorance  
  A. Quote: “It is kismet that makes us all have to go live … like savages.”  
     – Both accept the cult as a sacred necessity for planetary survival. They know it is artificial but have agreed to the ruse “forever,” demonstrating conscious sacrifice. Larhgan’s own “heart will be breaking” proves she suffers with full awareness, not naïveté.  

4. Public Denunciations Are Role-Playing, Not True Sentiments  
  A. Quote: “Go Away from me … A beggar does not associate with the high priestess.”  
     – Every aspect of “beggary” is part of the primitive charade. Later: “Hurry up, Skkiru … They mustn’t suspect the existence of the city underground or we’re finished before we’ve started.”  
     – Both silently know the real situation; his removal maintains cover for the “city underground.” Far from ignorance, they collectively preserve the secret mission.  

IV. Occam’s Razor and Consistency with Planetary Welfare  
  – My interpretation is the simplest: two educated, genuinely in-love individuals sacrifice their own happiness “for the welfare of Snaddra,” fully intending to resume normal life once the Earthmen’s study succeeds. No credible evidence of an alternative faction, no clandestine followers, and no overthrow occurs.  
  – Debater_B’s theory requires improbable surreptitious organization under the nose of heavily surveilling Earthmen, the despised Bbulas, and a populace trained to maintain primitive customs, all without a single slip or recruit.  

V. Conclusion  
Every explicit “fuzzed eye,” vow of celibacy, repeated obedience despite misery, and faithful cooperation “for the welfare of Snaddra” confirms that Skkiru and Larhgan endure in love, not as dupe and manipulator. My position best explains their sacrifices and mutual hope “forever.” Therefore, Skkiru and Larhgan remain devoted lovers tragically separated by necessity, not by deceit or secret plotting.
